podcast.body: The fifth single from "Morning Glory," this was the first Oasis single sung exclusively by Noel Gallagher. He wrote it on Tuesday, April 18, 1995, on a rainy night in Paris after returning from a strip club, while Oasis was opening for The Verve. Inspiration came from David Bowie's "All the Young Dudes" (performed by Mott the Hoople) and a bootlegged tape of John Lennon's memoirs (stolen after his murder on December 8, 1980), particularly Lennon's quote about "trying to start a revolution from me bed." The piano sounds also share similarities with Lennon's "Imagine" and "Watching the Wheels." Six days later, Liam Gallagher misheard Noel singing "Sally can wait" during a soundcheck for their first arena headlining gig in Sheffield; Noel, not having specific lyrics, then finished the song in the dressing room with the iconic "don't look back and anger." Noel performed it live acoustically hours later. "Sally" is ambiguous, possibly a nod to The Stone Roses' "Sally Cinnamon." Recorded in the same two-week span as "Wonderwall" in Wales, its official single release was February 19, 1996. It has since become a "second British national anthem," sung at funerals, weddings, and as a healing song after the Manchester concert bombing on May 22, 2017. "And it even became a healing song for the general public after the horrendous Manchester concert bombing on May 22nd, 2017."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song, featured on the album *(What's the Story) Morning Glory?*, has Noel Gallagher on lead vocals. It was the first Oasis single to feature Noel on lead and became the band's second single to reach number one on the British charts. Noel wrote the acoustic number quickly, drawing inspiration from David Bowie's 1979 song "Look Back in Anger" and a John Lennon bootleg, which explains the piano intro's similarity to "Imagine." Much of it was written during soundchecks while touring with The Verve, and Noel admitted to being "happily stoned" while writing the lyrics. "Good move too because the first Oasis single to feature Noel became the second Oasis single to reach number one on the British charts Oh The leader of the band, but the second voice in Oasis Noel Gallagher and don't look back an anger"
